reviews.review_title: Potential being held back by bugs
reviews.review_description:
Love the combat, but keeps switching player height. Also sometimes stutters & loses tracking for a split second. 

Using Quest 2 & Quest Pro controllers. Issue doesn't occur with any other apps. 

Inventory is also a bit of a mess & location of the pouch has trouble reacting to input. Despite the vibe you're going for, I'd suggest a backpack system for cleanliness. Beardo Benjo also mentioned the pouch issue in his PCVR impressions vid.

If you can sort this issues, you'll have a absolute winner on your hands. As it is, they sour the experience.

Edit: Discovered a loading bug when selecting continue after loading to main menu. Starts loading, Grimlord logo appears with sound cue, but then goes silent & freezes. Doesn't load any further despite waiting. Restart of app doesn't work. Only solution was fully powering off headset.

Other issue that may be bug or tracking issue, but intermittently & frequently shield or weapon doesn't block attack, despite being in the correct position, with full stamina. Mostly happens when close to enemy npcs.

reviews.review_description:
Making a game is hard, these guys are onto something and they and we know it.

This review is intended as a 'quick' fair guide on my experiences of what to expect (Jun 2023) to interested audiences.

1. It is not the full game but a sample, which isn't made clear anywhere. (I found it through beardobenjo's YouTube, somehow he had more of the game to play.)

2. Capitalises on and inspired by Dark Souls: yes. It is not Souls obviously, but has inspirations. The lack of instructions is actually ok, much of the controls are intuitive and you'll die a few times whilst teaching yourself (IE. Hint, hit the enemies where they DON'T have armour... = Ohhhhh!)

3. What to expect is to start in an empty space, find some weapons and eventually figure out a portal, teleport to one level in two parts, find enemies fight and progress. Very soulsy progression with deaths but determination. 
A few different enemies require slightly different tactics, but often you can dodge and then walk in and stab. 
They don't have health bars so sometimes you down them but they get back up, perhaps utilising an invisible stagger meter.
The eventual boss, is very simple by this point and too easily telegraphed, and you hit him forever (you'll be experienced by this point) and eventually he falls, and then there's not much else to do. In the (currently) empty hub, you can spawn basic weapons to try out, and I think this uses the gold you've collected from killing enemies. If you return to the boss room you're locked in and have to quit out.

4. Combat - is actually good. Enjoyably, (usually) so. 
Unlike many other games where wiggling your arms is as effective as realistic strikes, here the tracking is quite good, if you stab with your sword, or swing axe, and aren't careful sometimes your weapons are hitting each other. Blocking isn't always accurate, often i'd intentionally go to do so, and it wouldn't register, but it's debatable perhaps I wasn't at the right angle, or my stamina was too low or another unexplained rule as to why it didn't block. Part of the figuring out.
I do like that if you parry too much then your stamina is overfull and you drop your weapon. Good mechanic.

Spells - I didn't play enough, no guide as to what shapes to make and spells they create, I played a bit with ice, and waving a circle Forms a small shard, which fires like a bullet but did very little upon repeated use, so I switched back to melee.

Two handing - the grips look realistic, but not yet perfect with collision detection to make it as viable as one handed in my experience. Again no information on how two handing effects damage, and it's harder to parry (I found at least) than dual wielding.

My most effective so far was dual wielding two swords, one stabs the other chops and parries, whilst using the dodge technique.
I wanted to like the axe, but... Myah so far.

5. Glitches - the most common seems to be 'sticky hands' - semi often, whilst gripping weapons, and starting a level or interacting with a portal, the hands would get stuck to the level and you have to reload.
- Sometimes enemies get you through walls, yet your weapons bounce off realistically.
- sometimes your weapon gets stuck to a surface, you have to drop it and recollect it. That's ok though, can be annoying in combat, but adds to the tension.

6. Movement - it's quite slow, I don't know if my quest 2 controller is slightly buggy as doesn't always consistently move forward with left joystick on a few different games, and here the 'jump' seems purely vertical, I couldn't jump any gaps for example, so I could get over a few fences, or jump attack an enemy but I hadn't found it overly useful. 'sprint' is a tiny dash, useful in combat, doesn't seem to use stamina but also not spammable, so not sure the rules, seems every few seconds you can dash again.

7. Viewpoint - last to mention but not to be underrated, it's obviously POV, but the visualisation of the arms, body and legs is actually the vest I've seen. It doesn't get in the way, occasionally the interface with your weapon slots and potions pouch is a big annoying, IE. I couldn't sheath the weapon in my left hand (1h) on my right hip for example, as it kept thinking I wanted my potions pouch. So to use my hip slots, I had to use the same side hand. But overall good management style, with the vibration to know it's registered and to activate the action (IE put away / withdraw) which is positively intuitive.

Overall, very enjoyable and complex enough to be interested for the longer game, combat and difficulty were the highlight. Graphics and bugs will need work but gameplay will/ should always be the priority. I personally like the lack of instructions and think it should stay that way, I imagine with spells, we'll find scrolls that teach different shapes to use as we progress. (Would be cool if also includes the action & voice prompt!) But spells need to be viable compared to the melee, so we'll see I guess! Would also be nice to notice the difference between weapons, which perhaps I need to simply play more with 2h axe, vs 1h axe, vs 2h sword etc and the various effects of hitting different enemies to test if IE. The axe is better at staggering shielded enemies.

Looking forward to more. Always happy to playtest and provide balanced feedback.
And would love to add some proper narrative story. (That's my job!)
